sentences.text: The present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 seeks grant of parole for a period of three months and assails rejection order No. F.18/341/2018/HG/2828-2831, dated 18th September, 2025.
Parole is sought on medical grounds as the Petitioner requires regular follow-up treatment following insertion of a rod in his leg.

2. The Petitioner is a convict in FIR No. 97/2013 under Sections 363 & 376 of the IPC and Section 6 read with 5(M) of the POCSO Act, registered at P.S. Najafgarh and is undergoing rigorous imprisonment for 13 years.

sentences.text: The impugned order proceeds on the ground that the Petitioner had earlier violated the conditions of parole by not surrendering on time.

The record shows that he was initially released on 90 days' parole from 15 th May, 2021 to 14th August, 2021 and the period of emergency parole was thereafter extended from time to time until 7th April, 2023.

The Petitioner, however, did not surrender upon expiry of the extended period and was eventually re-arrested on 2nd August, 2024,
after a delay of nearly 01 year and 04 months.
5. The Petitioner contends that, owing to repeated extensions of emergency parole, he was not aware of the actual date on which he was required to surrender.
6. Although the delay in surrender on the part of the Petitioner is considerable, this Court has, in other matters involving emergency parole, taken a lenient view where similar delays have occurred.
Moreover, the nominal roll records that the Petitioner's conduct during the past one year has been satisfactory and that he is working as a Sahayak in jail.
His overall conduct has been graded unsatisfactory solely on account of the punishment imposed for delayed surrender.

7. In view of the above, and having regard to the Petitioner's medical condition, remaining sentence,
and the peculiar facts of the case, the request for parole is allowed.

8. The Petitioner is, accordingly, directed to be released for a period of four weeks, from the date of his release, on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of INR 10,000/- with one surety in the like amount to the
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/12/2025 at 22:17:27 satisfaction of the concerned Jail Superintendent, subject to the following conditions:
( i) The Petitioner shall report to the concerned SHO(s) once a week on every Monday during the period of parole.

(ii) The Petitioner shall furnish his telephone number to the SHO(s) concerned,
which the Petitioner will keep operational at all times.
(iii) The Petitioner shall surrender before the Jail Authorities at the expiry of the period of parole.
9. The petition is disposed of in the above terms along with pending application(s), if any.
10. A copy of the order be communicated to the concerned Jail Superintendent for information and necessary compliance.
